questions.prompt: What is most likely the diagnosis?
questions.modelAnswer: Acute rheumatic fever following untreated streptococcal pharyngitis

questions.prompt: What is the most likely causative organism, and what is its morphology on Gram stain?
What is the hemolytic pattern of this organism? Which test differentiates it from other organisms with similar morphology and hemolysis, and what is the expected result?
questions.modelAnswer: β-hemolytic; bacitracin sensitivity test; organism is bacitracin-sensitive

questions.prompt: This organism can cause a toxic shock-like syndrome. Which toxin is responsible for this?
What are the two major nonsuppurative sequelae of infection with this organism, and which type of infection is each associated with?
questions.modelAnswer: Acute rheumatic fever, follows pharyngitis only; Poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis, follows pharyngitis or skin infection (impetigo)

questions.prompt: What is the treatment of choice for pharyngitis caused by this organism?
What virulence factors of this organism promote immune evasion?
questions.modelAnswer: Hyaluronic acid capsule: interferes with phagocytosis. M protein: blocks the binding of complement compoent C3b -> impair phagocytosis.

questions.prompt: Explain the pathophysiology of this patient's condition and identify the type of hypersensitivity reaction involved.
questions.modelAnswer: Molecular mimicry: antibodies against M protein cross-react with host tissues (heart, joints, CNS), leading to inflammation; this is a type II hypersensitivity reaction

questions.prompt: [Extra] Why are antistreptolysin O (ASO) titers used instead of antibodies to streptolysin S? Name one additional laboratory test that can detect prior infection.
questions.modelAnswer: Streptolysin O is antigenic, therefore can cause the body to produce antibodies against this toxin. On the other hand, streptolysin S is not antigenic, so there is no production of antibodies against this toxin, so it cannot be used as a diagnostic test for past *Streptococcus pyogenes* infections. Some other diagnostic tests are anti-DNase B and anti-hyaluronidase for example.
